original_concern.concern: Proof 3.1 says the complement-cover identification extends smoothly because it preserves boundary monodromies. Monodromy alone supplies no smooth extension across a square branch chart: for example, a nonconformal real-linear normal germ generally has no differentiable square-root lift. The argument needs an explicit tubular normalization or compatible transported branch charts, including the claimed independence from arbitrary tubular charts in 2.1. The isotopy-invariance conclusion is standard, but this smoothness step is not justified as written.

original_native_verdict_preserved.reason: No fatal defect found: Alexander duality and Hurewicz give the stated meridian character; the local model matches both monodromies, and the isotopy carries its kernel to the corresponding kernel, allowing the cover isomorphism to extend across the branch tubes.

cases.decision_basis: Smooth extension gap; original Statement retained.
cases.reasoning: Equality of monodromies classifies covers only away from the branch core. For example A(x+iy)=2x+iy is orientation preserving but not complex conformal. A differentiable lift h of A(z²) under squaring would have a real-linear invertible derivative B with (Bz)²=A(z²); writing Bz=az+b conjugate(z), the missing |z|² coefficient forces ab=0, and orientation then forces b=0, inconsistent with the conjugate(z)² coefficient of A(z²). Thus the current claimed extension is unjustified. The proposal normalizes tubes to a rotation by equal-normal-derivative tubular uniqueness and a positive-definite polar homotopy, then supplies an actual smooth square-root phase. For isotopy invariance it first transports charts. The Statement remains the same oriented total-space diffeomorphism assertion; no stronger smooth isomorphism over a fixed identity base map is asserted.

proposals.source_excerpt: 2.1 By [F3] and [F4], the index-two kernel determines a connected two-sheeted cover. On the boundary of a punctured tube around $K_i$, its two monodromies are the prescribed meridian value $1$ and a longitude value $\eta_i\in\mathbb F_2$. The local model [F5] has exactly those two monodromies; classification of covers of the punctured tube identifies it with the restricted cover. The displayed model therefore extends the cover across every branch component. If a tubular framing is changed by $k$ meridional twists, the parallel longitude changes by $k\mu_i$, so its character changes by $k$ modulo two; the corresponding rotation of the normal coordinate changes the phase in the local model by the same parity. Thus these are coordinate descriptions of one extension, not different covers. [F3, F4, F5, step 1.1]
proposals.proposed_replacement:
2.1 By [F3] and [F4], the index-two kernel determines a connected two-sheeted cover. On a punctured tube around $K_i$, its two monodromies are the meridian value $1$ and a longitude value $\eta_i\in\mathbb F_2$. The local model [F5] has exactly these monodromies, so covering classification identifies its punctured part with the restricted cover. Attach its core to obtain a smooth extension in the chosen charts. This constructs an extension; independence of the smooth total-space diffeomorphism type requires the normalization below, not merely equality of boundary monodromies. [F3, F4, F5, step 1.1]

2.2 Compare two oriented tubular charts $\varphi_0,\varphi_1$ around the same component. Express them over a common oriented core parameter $s$; a change of the original core parameter only replaces the unit phase $e^{\mathrm i\eta_j s}$ by a smooth unit loop $a_j(s)$ of the same winding number $\eta_j$. Let $A(s)\in GL^+(2,\mathbb R)$ be the unique vertical linear change for which $\varphi_1\circ A$ and $\varphi_0$ induce the same normal-quotient identification. Write $A=RP$ by smooth polar decomposition, with $R(s)\in SO(2)$ and $P(s)$ positive definite. The compatible-tube assertion [F6] gives an ambient isotopy fixing the core and carrying $\varphi_0$ to $\varphi_1\circ A$ near it. The fiber-linear isotopy $R((1-t)P+tI)$ then connects $A$ to $R$ through invertible maps. On a common smaller tube its composition with $\varphi_1$ is an isotopy of open embeddings, with open track, fixing the core. The relative open-set clause of [F6] extends it near the compact core. Thus an ambient diffeomorphism $g$, isotopic to the identity through maps fixing the whole link, satisfies $g\circ\varphi_0=\varphi_1\circ R$ near this component. Choose the supports in disjoint component tubes and compose the finitely many isotopies. [F6, given, construct]

2.3 Identify $R(s)$ with a unit complex number, of winding $k$. The image under $g$ of the first chart longitude has slope $\lambda_1+k\mu$ in the second chart, so preservation of the meridian character gives $\eta_0\equiv\eta_1+k\pmod2$. The unit loop $R(s)a_0(s)/a_1(s)$ therefore has even winding. It has a smooth periodic square root $r(s)$: lift its argument on $[0,2\pi]$, halve it, and use even winding to match the endpoints and derivatives. In the two branch models $b_j(s,z)=(s,a_j(s)z^2)$ the map $(s,z)\mapsto(s,r(s)z)$ consequently covers $g$, since $a_1r^2=Ra_0$. It is an orientation-preserving smooth diffeomorphism including $z=0$. The two signs of $r$ differ by the deck map. Choose the sign matching the complement-cover isomorphism at one point of each connected punctured tube; covering uniqueness makes them agree throughout that tube. Hence the local lifts glue to the complement lift. This proves independence of the oriented smooth total-space diffeomorphism type from arbitrary oriented tubular charts. It does not assert a smooth lift over the identity base map between arbitrary unnormalized charts. [F4, F5, step 1.1, step 2.2, construct, algebra]

proposals.source_excerpt: 3.1 The based covering uniqueness in [F4] identifies the two complement covers over this diffeomorphism. The identification extends over each branch tube because it preserves the two boundary monodromies in step 2.1; the local order-two models then give an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of the closed branched covers. Thus $\Sigma(L')\cong\Sigma(L)$ as oriented manifolds. [F4, F5, step 2.1, step 1.2] ∎
proposals.proposed_replacement: 3.1 Let $F$ be the terminal diffeomorphism of the given ambient isotopy from $L$ to $L'$. First choose the target tubular charts by transporting the source charts through $F$. Corresponding longitudes have the same character, and in these transported branch coordinates a lift is $(s,z)\mapsto(s,z)$, or its deck translate. By step 1.2 and [F4] the complement covers are isomorphic over $F$; on every punctured tube that isomorphism is one of these two local lifts, so it extends smoothly across the branch core. The resulting map is an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of the closed total spaces. Finally steps 2.2–2.3 compare the transported target charts with any originally chosen target charts. Thus $\Sigma(L')\cong\Sigma(L)$ as oriented manifolds, with no unjustified smooth extension of an arbitrary normal germ. [F4, F5, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 2.3] ∎

proposals.source_excerpt: [F5] The local normal-disk model for a branch component is $(s,z)\mapsto(s,e^{\mathrm i\eta s}z^2)$ with $s\in\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$; its meridian monodromy is nontrivial and its longitudinal monodromy is $\eta\in\mathbb F_2$ ([[def-double-branched-cover-of-an-oriented-link]]).
proposals.proposed_replacement:
[F5] The local normal-disk model for a branch component is $(s,z)\mapsto(s,e^{\mathrm i\eta s}z^2)$ with $s\in\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$; its meridian monodromy is nontrivial and its longitudinal monodromy is $\eta\in\mathbb F_2$ ([[def-double-branched-cover-of-an-oriented-link]]).

[F6] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, two tubular embeddings of the same normal bundle inducing the same vertical normal-quotient map are ambient isotopic near a compact core, fixing that core ([[cor-tubular-neighbourhoods-are-unique-up-to-ambient-isotopy]]). The relative open-set clause of [[thm-isotopy-extension]] also extends an isotopy of an ambient open set with open track near any compact subset. In the application the ambient manifold is the boundaryless $S^3$, the core is the compact union of link circles, the normal identifications are explicitly equalized, and the fiber-linear isotopy consists of open embeddings after a common shrinking. AC implies the required countable choice.

proposals.source_excerpt: For every integer $k\ge1$, let $U_k\subset S^3$ be a $k$-component planar unlink with an arbitrary orientation on each component, and choose a basepoint $p$ on any one component. Its double branched cover is $\#^{\,k-1}(S^2\times S^1)$, with $\Sigma(U_1)=S^3$. Over $\mathbb F_2$, the hat Floer group of this cover is identified with the exterior algebra on a $(k-1)$-dimensional vector space, hence has rank $2^{k-1}$. Under these identifications, the cobordism maps for saddle cobordisms between neighboring unlink resolutions, with $p$ carried outside the saddle disk, are the multiplication and comultiplication maps of the two-dimensional Frobenius algebra $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$ after reduction at the marked component. The identification includes the marked-circle cases and fixes the basis conventions needed to compare the first surgery differential with the reduced Khovanov cube.
